item.title: Behind the Wealth and Princeton Degree Was a Family Heading for Tragedy
item.description:
Thomas Gilbert Jr., a Princeton graduate, shot his wealthy hedge-fund manager father in their Manhattan apartment in January 2015. He had asked his mother to leave and buy him a can of Coke. When she returned around 15 minutes later, his father was dead, and the scene appeared staged to suggest suicide. Prosecutors argued the killing followed a dispute over his allowance. Gilbert was convicted of second-degree murder in 2019 and sentenced to 30 years to life.
Was the Coke request part of the plan to get his mother out of the apartment?

item.title: A Brutal Attack That Nearly Cost a Woman Her Life
item.description: A woman’s walk to work in Melbourne turned terrifying when a stranger attacked her from behind. CCTV captured the incident and a bystander rushing to help. Lauren Darul was later charged over the attack.
